text:
Mason Marchment is on his sixth NHL team at 31, an undrafted winger who keeps getting traded for and keeps producing, and he scored his 100th NHL goal for San Jose against Pittsburgh on Nov. 11. San Jose Hockey Now wrote on Nov. 16 that he and Dmitry Orlov are finding their games, and the last week backs it up: a four-game point streak, the shootout winner against Utah, then a power-play goal and an assist in Calgary.

He has 6 goals and 12 points in 24 games, and the goals sit right on his chances. His ice time is up nearly two minutes over the last ten games. Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest singled out his back-door pass to Gaudette against Calgary, and the playmaking has been there all along.

The bigger issue is around him. San Jose gets about 41% of the expected goals in his five-on-five minutes, and his linemates have finished about four goals under their chances. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.5 wins in 2025-26, 85th percentile at taking chances away, so the defensive numbers here are worse than his history. Watch the five-on-five share: if it climbs, his points will too.
